speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
question: Why not delight in variety?
premises: Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise, dissolution, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining-forth, universe-bodied — are not different-natured.
Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded (avekṣya) that-that (tattattad) one-self-natured (ekātmatā) consciousness-form (saṃvidrūpam) —
Why (kiṃ na) do you delight (ramase), full (nirbharaḥ) of that contemplation (tadbhāvanā)?
Regard is the whole practice: see variety as one-self-natured consciousness-form — delight is the only consistent response.
inference: Variety is one nature; regard it as consciousness-form, and delight is the only consistent response.
uncertainties: Whether 'ekātmatāsaṃvidrūpa' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'ramase' is indicative or imperative is unresolved.
